signals.signal: Optima's ENTIRE network-security estate is Fortinet, revealed by its own open vacancy 'Network engineer - Fortinet specialist | Infrastructure | IT operations' (IT department, Athens): FortiGate NGFW clusters in Active-Active/Active-Passive HA with SD-WAN, FortiWeb (WAF), FortiADC (load balancer), FortiMail (email security gateway), FortiAuthenticator, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, plus site-to-site IPSec/SSL VPN tunnels between data centres and branches; requires Fortinet NSE 4 and optionally NSE 5 (FortiManager & FortiAnalyzer), 10+ years' experience, and ISO 27001/GDPR compliance familiarity.
signals.source_name: Optima bank careers portal, job posting 'Network engineer - Fortinet specialist' (recovered via the site's Umbraco jobs API /umbraco/api/optimaapi/getjobslist)
signals.implies: This scopes the open 'firewall management and network security policy platform' evaluation Optima disclosed in its FY2025 report: any bid must manage a Fortinet estate (FortiManager-native, or a Tufin/AlgoSec-class policy-orchestration overlay). It converts a vague procurement signal into a concrete, technically-qualified Printec security/managed-services proposal, and confirms Optima buys network security as products plus outside expertise rather than building it.
signals.followup: Approach the CISO/IT Operations with a Fortinet-native firewall-policy-management and DLP-implementation proposition; confirm whether either selection has already been awarded (neither is mentioned in the 1H26 pack).

signals.signal: TWO NAMED OPEN VENDOR SELECTIONS in the FY2025 report: (1) 'Data Classification has been completed and the Group is in the process of selecting a partner to implement advanced DLP solutions to prevent unauthorized data extraction' (alongside Azure Information Protection); (2) 'Firewall Management and Network Security Policy Platform: The Group evaluates candidate platforms to determine their suitability for firewall management and network security policy requirements.' Also disclosed: DORA compliance project 'at an advanced stage of implementing corrective actions'; ISO 27001:2022 certified by LRQA in 2025; a 24/7 SOC + SIEM, EDR/AV on all endpoints, third-party MDR services, WAF, email sandboxing, a full Disaster Recovery site, regular penetration/vulnerability testing and periodic red-teaming.
signals.source_name: Optima bank FY2025 Annual Financial Report (group and bank), cybersecurity/system-failure section
signals.implies: The warmest Printec door at Optima, and it sits in the security/managed-services line rather than ATM. Two live procurements plus DORA remediation, on top of an already outsourced SOC/SIEM/MDR posture, mark Optima as an established buyer of third-party ICT-security services despite its tiny capex.
signals.followup: Pair the DLP-partner pitch with the Fortinet policy-management finding; ask for the DORA register-of-information gap list as the door-opener.

signals.signal: ACCESSIBILITY GAP stated in Optima's own words on a dedicated public page. The accessibility statement claims Optima 'has complied with Law 4994/2022 and Directive (EU) 2019/882' (the European Accessibility Act), yet the only estate commitment is that 'the majority of the bank's ATMs are accessible from wheelchairs'. The FY2025 report repeats 'Most ATMs are wheelchair accessible' and 'The majority of branches ensure easy access for people with mobility difficulties'; the 1H2026 IR presentation quantifies only '60% of branches accessible to PWD'. There is NO claim anywhere of audio/voice-guided ATMs; the text-to-speech tool is a document reader available at selected branches, and Braille statements are 'upon request'.
signals.source_name: Optima bank accessibility statement (optimabank.gr) + FY2025 Annual Financial Report + 1H2026 IR presentation ESG slide
signals.implies: Every large Greek peer claims 100% voice-guided ATMs (NBG 837 units end-2025 targeting 100% by end-2026; Alpha delivered by Printec since 2021; Eurobank 100%). Optima claims none while publicly asserting EAA/Law 4994/2022 compliance, on an estate of only c.29 machines. That is a small, cheap, reputationally urgent retrofit and is precisely the ATM accessibility/voice-guidance scope Printec already delivered at Alpha Bank.
signals.likelihood: Medium - peer and regulatory pressure rising, no programme announced
signals.followup: Identify the ATM OEM/software on the 29 units to size a voice-guidance retrofit; check Greek enforcement of Law 4994/2022 for self-service terminals and whether any authority has opened a review of bank ATM accessibility.

signals.signal: ATM estate confirmed twice over. The interim report states: 'Each branch of the Bank's network has an external automatic teller machine (ATM) to serve customers who wish to use their debit/credit cards to make cash withdrawals or balance inquiries.' Independently, the Greek branch-locator page returns 32 location pages of which exactly 29 carry an 'ATM post' tag. The bank operated 30 branches at 30/06/2026 (21 Athens, 3 Thessaloniki, 1 Corinth, 1 Larissa, 1 Patras, 2 Crete, 1 Komotini), flat at 30 for five consecutive quarters (29 in 2Q25, then 30 in 3Q25/4Q25/1Q26/2Q26).
signals.source_name: Optima bank interim financial statements 30/06/2026 (ATM and branch sections) + optimabank.gr branch-network locator HTML + 1H2026 IR presentation branch series
signals.implies: Printec's ATM/self-service hardware TAM at Optima is c.29-30 through-the-wall units, zero off-site fleet, withdrawal and balance enquiry only - explicitly NO cash-in or recycling. The cash-automation/TCR opportunity is effectively nil; the only credible play is a managed-services / ATM-as-a-service wrap on the existing units.
signals.followup: Identify the ATM OEM (never disclosed) and the current field-service provider; test whether Optima would outsource the whole 29-unit estate end-to-end.

signals.signal: Brand-new tariff editions in force 20/07/2026 (Basic tariff ANX158.55/20-07-2026 and electronic-transactions tariff ANX216.31/20-07-2026) confirm Optima's ATMs generate no revenue: debit-card cash withdrawals cost EUR 0 at Optima's own ATMs AND at all other banks' ATMs in Greece/EEA; EUR 0.75 at third-party ATM-network operators in Greece/EEA (EUR 0 in municipal units that have only one ATM, or in municipalities composed only of such units); EUR 0.75 outside Greece/EEA. Several card fees are flagged as taking effect 01/09/2026.
signals.source_name: Optima bank, Basic Tariff of Commissions and Other Charges, edition ANX158.55
signals.implies: Under the Greek ATM fee regime (zero on own network, capped third-party fees since 11/08/2025) Optima's 29 machines earn nothing while serving rivals' customers for free - a pure cost centre carried purely for branch presence. That is the single strongest commercial argument for selling Optima a fixed-fee managed-ATM / ATM-as-a-service contract instead of ownership.
signals.followup: Build a total-cost-of-ownership comparison for 29 units (cash-in-transit, servicing, compliance, accessibility retrofit) versus a Printec managed-service fee, and take it to the COO.

signals.signal: H1 2026 results (published 30/07/2026): net profit EUR 104.3m vs EUR 81.1m in 1H25 (+29%); pre-provision profit EUR 142.9m vs EUR 108.1m; pre-tax profit EUR 127.7m; total regulatory capital EUR 1,088.5m bank / EUR 1,112.2m group on RWAs of EUR 6,102.2m / EUR 6,401.9m, giving a total capital ratio of 17.84% bank / 17.37% group; LCR 144.27% and NSFR 123.52% at bank level. Cost-to-core-income 22.6% for 1H26 (2Q26 alone 22.0%) versus 25.5% in 1H25 and 23.2% in 1Q26. FY2026 guidance RAISED: net profit from >EUR 195m to >EUR 210m, loan growth from +EUR 1.1bn to +EUR 1.35bn, deposit growth from +EUR 1.4bn to +EUR 1.7bn, cost of risk 55bps, cost-to-core-income <30%. Guidance explicitly excludes any Euroxx impact. Branch NPS 87.55 (12-month rolling).
signals.source_name: Optima bank, condensed interim financial statements 30 June 2026 and 1H2026 IR presentation
signals.implies: Optima has ample earnings power and capital headroom to buy technology, but it is deploying capital into the loan book while defending a sub-23% cost ratio. Any Printec proposition must be framed as opex-light managed services that protect that ratio, never as an equipment purchase.
signals.followup: Watch for a first-ever Capital Markets Day or any technology-spend disclosure; the guidance beat suggests appetite to fund a step-change once Euroxx closes.

signals.signal: Capex remains structurally tiny and is FALLING. FY2025: additions to fixed assets EUR 1.9m (2024: EUR 1.8m); additions to intangible assets EUR 3.1m (2024: EUR 3.7m) - a total of c.EUR 5.0m against EUR 170m FY2025 net profit. 1H 2026: fixed-asset additions EUR 737k (1H25: EUR 769k); intangible additions EUR 1.1m (1H25: EUR 1.2m). 1H26 depreciation and amortisation of EUR 4.6m is attributed mainly to right-of-use buildings and multi-year expenses, not equipment.
signals.source_name: Optima bank FY2025 Annual Financial Report and condensed interim financial statements 30/06/2026
signals.implies: Hard evidence that no hardware-refresh or fleet-expansion budget exists at Optima. Any Printec deal must be sized in the low hundreds of thousands of euro per year and structured as subscription/managed service (security software, ATM-as-a-service) rather than capitalised equipment.
signals.followup: Re-check 9M-2026 and FY2026 additions for any step-up tied to Euroxx integration.

signals.signal: Euroxx acquisition timeline firmed to year-end: the 1H2026 IR presentation (30/07/2026) states Euroxx is 'On track with timeframe; expected completion by YE 26'. Optima's board approved a non-binding offer on 17/03/2026 for 67%-80.84% of Euroxx for up to EUR 65.5m; Euroxx is the third-largest Greek investment firm with a 12.4% brokerage market share in 2025, and management has guided to c.10% uplift in commission income. Notably, Euroxx is NOT mentioned anywhere in the 1H26 interim financial statements notes pack - no commitment and no subsequent-event note - i.e. it is still not contractually closed, and FY2026 guidance excludes it.
signals.source_name: Optima bank 1H2026 IR presentation (30/07/2026); Optima bank interim financial statements 30/06/2026 (silence on Euroxx); Greek financial press on the March 2026 board approval
signals.implies: A 4Q26/1Q27 integration window that bolts a brokerage, investment-banking and asset-management business onto Optima, bringing market-abuse surveillance, suitability monitoring, trade surveillance and a materially wider AML/KYC surface. This is the realistic entry point for Printec AML/compliance and transaction monitoring, and for extending eKYC to investment-services onboarding.
signals.followup: Time an AML/market-abuse-monitoring and investment-onboarding pitch to the close; watch for the HCMC approval and any tender for surveillance tooling. Optima already runs an 'Optima bank trader' platform and a Brokerage department that is itself hiring.

signals.signal: Optima's live vacancy list (21 open roles at 30/07/2026) shows where the organisation is being built: 'AML/CFT & Authorities Investigations' (Compliance), 'Junior IT auditor', 'Project manager, Officer - IT', 'Microsoft 365 & Azure specialist - Mid level', 'IT Operations - Junior level', 'Network engineer - Fortinet specialist', 'Officer - Risk management', plus 'Institutional & Global Brokers - Officer' in a Brokerage department. There is NOT a single ATM, self-service, cash-operations or branch-hardware role in the list. Headcount reached 626 bank / 663 group at 30/06/2026, from 573 / 605 a year earlier.
signals.source_name: Optima bank careers portal jobs list (Umbraco API /umbraco/api/optimaapi/getjobslist) + interim financial statements 30/06/2026 headcount note
signals.implies: Two readings for Printec. First, the AML/CFT and risk hiring lands exactly on the Bank of Greece's stated 2026 supervisory priority of on-site inspection of customer transaction-monitoring systems, and ahead of AMLR application in July 2027 - a compliance/transaction-monitoring window. Second, the total absence of self-service roles confirms Optima has no internal ATM organisation at all, which makes a fully outsourced managed-ATM service the only viable route, but also means there is no internal champion for it.
signals.followup: Map the AML/CFT function's current monitoring tooling; a bank with no dedicated ATM staff is a natural full-outsourcing prospect - test with the COO.

signals.signal: Capital raised is funding growth and M&A, not estate. EUR 200m inaugural Additional Tier 1 issued 10/06/2026 (perpetual, callable after 5 years, coupon 6.75%, book above EUR 2.2bn, 11x oversubscribed, listed on the Luxembourg Euro MTF), confirmed in the interim statements. This follows the EUR 500m EMTN programme established in 2025 with an inaugural EUR 150m Tier 2 reset note at 5.5% due 25/09/2035 (ISIN XS3104415545, 10.25NC5.25), also 11x oversubscribed; the EMTN programme has since been refreshed with a 2026 Offering Circular published on the bank's IR site.
signals.source_name: Optima bank interim financial statements 30/06/2026 (AT1 note); DLA Piper transaction announcement on the EUR 150m Tier 2 / EMTN establishment; Optima bank investor-relations EMTN document list
signals.implies: Context only: funding capacity is being built for lending and for the Euroxx acquisition, reinforcing that hardware is not the use of proceeds. Useful for framing a services-not-capex pitch.
signals.followup: Monitor the refreshed 2026 EMTN programme for senior-preferred/MREL issuance that could fund an acquisition-driven IT programme.

signals.signal: Digital stack re-verified as third-party but already installed: the NETinfo Digital Banking platform went live at Optima via NETinfo's partner Profile Software, which supplied an 'integration layer' on the WSO2 platform connecting the digital-banking front end to the core banking system and other bank systems. Current channel scope disclosed in the 1H26 interim report includes fully online account opening via remote identification (digital onboarding/eKYC) delivering a deposit account, debit card and e-banking access, Google Pay and Apple Pay, digital card lifecycle actions (activation, loss/re-issue, PIN sending, temporary lock/unlock), e-statements, push-notification transaction approval and live chat.
signals.source_name: Profile Software press release on the Optima bank go-live; Optima bank interim financial statements 30/06/2026 (digital banking section)
signals.implies: Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC line is foreclosed at Optima - the capability is live and owned by NETinfo/Profile on WSO2. Attacking it head-on is a losing bid; the realistic adjacency is compliance tooling behind the onboarding flow (sanctions/PEP, transaction monitoring) rather than the onboarding journey itself.
signals.followup: Confirm whether the NETinfo/Profile stack is contracted through to 2027+ and whether Euroxx integration forces a channel re-platforming.

coverage_notes: Full fresh pass (no valid JSON checkpoint existed; an interrupted-run .md from earlier the same day was present and its facts were re-derived from primary sources so that every row carries a citable URL). Primary sources opened and text-extracted locally with pdfminer: the 1H2026 interim notes full pack (30/07/2026), the 1H2026 IR presentation and press release, the FY2025 annual financial report (31/12/2025), and both current tariff editions (ANX158.55 and ANX216.31, in force 20/07/2026). New source environments used this run that previous runs did not touch: (a) the bank's Umbraco careers API, which yielded the full 21-role vacancy list and the Fortinet-specialist job description naming the whole network-security estate; (b) the raw HTML of the Greek branch-locator, which independently corroborated 29 'ATM post' tags across 32 location pages; (c) the standalone public accessibility statement at /support-area/prosvasimotita/, which yielded the Law 4994/2022 and Directive (EU) 2019/882 compliance claim alongside the qualified 'majority of ATMs are wheelchair accessible' wording. Searched in both English and Greek. Genuine gaps that remain: the ATM OEM/vendor on the 29 units is still unidentified anywhere in public sources and remains a standing task; no field-service provider is named; no AML/transaction-monitoring vendor is named; no Bank of Greece sanction or enforcement action against Optima was found (the BoG sanctions register lists no Optima entry surfaced by search, so absence is reported as not-found rather than as a negative finding); Optima publishes no IT-spend line, so software capex can only be inferred from intangible additions; Optima has no acquiring business and no POS estate, so the POS/acquiring line is genuinely empty rather than under-researched.
